chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said:
I asked Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), saying: 'A man has a eunuch who enters upon his womenfolk, and he gives them the wudu, so he sees their hair.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى: Abu Al-Hasan Musa (Imam Musa al-Kazim, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Does a eunuch seeing a woman's hair invalidate her wudu?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the fiqh of ritual purity regarding eunuchs (*khassa*), ruling that their gaze during a woman's ablution does not invalidate her state of purity. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes the eunuch's status from that of free men, particularly regarding the requirement of *awrah* concealment and the validity of prayer, reflecting the nuanced legal treatment of those with diminished sexual potency in household dynamics.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Is’haq who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> saying, ‘The man happens to have a eunuch for him, who enters upon his womenfolk, so he gives them (water for) the ablution, so he sees their hair’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Muhammad ibn Ishaq who has said the following: “

I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who has a castrated slave; if he can go to his women and provide them water for wudu and look at their hairs. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, he can do so.”’
